Alternate Future C9 Chevrolet Corvette Still Has an Engine But Also New Space-Age Design Traits
7 photos
Photo: t__mjh /Instagram
It’s been ‘a minute’ since General Motors approved the Corvette project back in 1953, and over the course of eight generations it has grown and even overshadowed its role as ‘America’s quintessential sports car,’ especially after it switched to the C8 iteration.
The Chevrolet Corvette only experienced two major shocks during its lifetime – once when it switched from the inaugural C1 design to the classic style introduced with the C2, and the second time when the established front-engine RWD setup was thrown down the drain for a new mid-engine platform with the introduction of the C8.
After that, innovations and records flowed: the Z06 has the most powerful naturally aspirated V8 ever made for production models, the 2027 Stingray and Grand Sport have the new 6.7-liter V8 with the most torque of any such NA engine (520 lb-ft of torque, 705 Nm), while the twin-turbo ZR1 and hybrid ZR1X have obviously entered supercar territory with their powerful 1,064-hp and 1,250-hp powertrains.
As such, it’s no wonder that everyone keeps a close eye on the past, present, and future of the Chevrolet Corvette – just recently, a new report from across the rumor mill claims that the Corvette SUV and sedan might not happen, after all, as GM thinks about going against the possibility of diluting the nameplate’s seven decades of sports car legacy.
Also, the members of the imaginative guild of digital car content creators dwelling across the parallel universes of vehicular CGI always seem to have an opinion about the past, present, and future of the Corvette. For example, Tom Hylton, an Exterior and Interior Designer for GAC Milano also moonlights as a virtual artist under the guise of ' t__mjh ' on social media.
Not long ago, his unofficial, hypothetical design project dubbed ‘ Product of Environment – USA ’ featured no less than five different vehicle designs (a fresh Peterbilt truck concept, a three-wheel “City Box,” a Caddy coupe, and a single-seater prototype) and also included the grand finale of an alternate timeline Chevrolet Corvette that’s contemporary with us but looked both retro and futuristic at the same time and kept the V8 firmly planted under the front hood.
Now he again muses about a potential Chevy Corvette, maybe the upcoming C9 iteration, and this time around it’s a mid-engine version as far as we can tell. It’s appropriate for the New Space Age in terms of design, with minimalistic lines and a low cabin that still includes two big-sized leather-wrapped bucket seats.
The wedge shape reminds us of Lamborghini, but it won’t be accused of copying any of the Italian supercars due to the quirky rear, which includes a tiny vertical rear window to go along with the pointy back design, the slim LED taillights, plus the singular oval exhaust outlet. So, this project is either ICE or HEV, not all-electric, for sure. Cool or not? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Tom (@t__mjh)
